newsitem.title: USA: States, localities outline litigation reform fears.
newsitem.headline: States, localities outline litigation reform fears.

text.p: Six state and local government groups warned a key U.S. Senate panel chairman Thursday to reject a new round of reforms that could restrict certain securities class actions in state courts.

"We urge you to oppose any efforts to interfere with the ability of states to protect public investors and taxpayers through the preemption of private securities fraud actions under state law," the National League of Cities and other groups said in a letter to Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, R-N.Y., chairman of the Senate Banking Committee.

The Committee's subpanel on securities Thursday heard the views of the securities industry, technology companies and others that want Congress to enact more curbs on "frivolous" lawsuits, including those landing in state courts.
In 1995, Congress enacted reforms over a presidential veto designed to restrict such suits, but many industry groups say litigators have gotten around the reforms by taking cases to state courts.
But the six groups warned D'Amato that some proposals under consideration would create insurmountable "hurdles" to recovery by state and local government investors, employees and taxpayers.
Examples are "loser pay" plans or expanded "safe harbors" for forward-looking financial statements, they said.
They added that curbing state court action would violate fundamental principles of federalism. "The federal government must tread carefully to avoid usurping state powers," the groups warned.

"(Our) governments must be able to protect state and local funds and taxpayers regardless of obstacles present in federal law," groups added. They pointed to legal protections that are currently unavailable under federal law.
Examples are sanctions for people who aid and abet securities law violators, longer statutes of limitations and joint and several liability, groups said.
The six groups told D'Amato that they were writing because no state or local government group was invited to testify at Thursday's hearing.

Other groups signing the letter were the National Association of Counties, National Assocation of County Treasurers and Finance Officers, Municipal Treasurers' Association, Government Finance Officers Association, and U.S. Conference of Mayors.
